briefs.about: The Dow Jones Industrial Average tracks 30 big, well-known US companies, like Apple, JPMorgan, Walmart and Nvidia. Higher-priced stocks count more, so a few members can move it a lot.
briefs.whyMoved: The Dow fell 1,101.11 points, or 2.19%, on Thursday to 49,097.06, its fourth loss in a row, and is moving closer to a 10% drop from its high; it was 53,356.12 on November 4, so it has lost about 4,259 points in two weeks. Dow members Nvidia (down 3.3%), Amazon (down 3.87%) and Microsoft (down 1.97%) fell with AI stocks, and factory and transport companies fell 2.61%. Walmart, another member, slipped 1.0% even after third-quarter sales of $188.8 billion, up 5.2%. Because the Dow holds only 30 companies, a few big drops pull the whole average down hard.

watch.what: PCE inflation report: experts expect core prices up 3.2% from a year ago; a higher number would raise rate-hike fears, a lower one could ease them.
Fed rate decision: traders put about a 96% chance on a quarter-point hike; a half-point hike would likely hit stocks harder, while a calm message could help.

briefs.name: Russell 2000
briefs.headline: Russell 2000 drops 2.18% to 2,655 as rate fears hit smaller companies
briefs.summary: The index stayed below the 2,700 level, which it slipped under earlier in the week and has struggled to win back. Insmed, a smaller drugmaker, jumped 20.58% on reports that Sanofi may buy it. Vivid Seats soared 63% after lenders agreed to swap about $273 million of debt for about 80% of its stock. More than 4 stocks fell for every 1 that rose on the New York Stock Exchange.
bull: Insmed jumped 20.58% on buyout talk from Sanofi, a reminder that big companies still pay up for promising small ones.
Jobless claims were a low 203,000, a sign the economy smaller companies depend on is still hiring.
The 10-year Treasury rate dipped about 2 points to 5.05%, and lower rates help small companies that borrow a lot.
bear: Traders put a 96.4% chance on a December Fed hike, which would raise loan costs for small companies the most.
A Philadelphia factory survey fell to 6.3 from 20.9, a warning that smaller, US-focused businesses may see fewer orders.
The index closed below 2,700 again, a level it has failed to win back this week, showing buyers are staying away.

briefs.about: The Russell 2000 tracks about 2,000 smaller US companies, such as regional banks, small factories and young health companies. It shows how smaller businesses are doing compared with giants.
briefs.whyMoved: The Russell 2000 fell 2.18%, or 59.20 points, on Thursday to 2,655.11, wiping out Wednesday's small gain to 2,714.31; it was 2,856.95 on November 4, so smaller companies are down about 7.1% in two weeks. It was already down 1.19% at midday as early hope around Anthropic's debut faded and health care and energy-linked stocks fell, then the selling grew into the close. Smaller companies borrow more of their money, often at rates that change, so the chance of a December Fed hike hits their profits harder than it hits giants with lots of cash.

watch.what: PCE inflation report: experts expect core prices up 3.2% from a year ago; a higher number would raise rate-hike fears, a lower one could ease them.
Fed rate decision: traders put about a 96% chance on a quarter-point hike; a half-point hike would likely hit stocks harder, while a calm message could help.

briefs.headline: Micron slips to $705.27 even after Nvidia's record quarter
briefs.about: Micron makes memory chips, the parts that store data in computers, phones and the giant data centers that run AI. Its main products are DRAM and NAND flash memory, plus HBM, a fast memory built for AI chips.
briefs.summary: Micron is still up about 147% in 2026 but is 41.9% below its June 25 high. Analysts expect sales to more than double to about $278 billion next fiscal year, with $175.61 of profit per share, so the stock costs only about 4 times this year's expected profit. Micron raised its stock buyback plan to $35.2 billion in October, and big buybacks can start December 9 under its government chip-grant rules. Micron also has 26 long-term customer deals covering more than 35% of its expected sales through 2030.
bull: Nvidia's part-buying promises rose to $390 billion from $279 billion, mostly multi-year memory deals, a direct sign of future demand for Micron's chips.
Raymond James expects Micron to spend over $100 billion a year buying back its own stock, which leaves fewer shares and more profit per share.
Micron made $32.9 billion of free cash (money left after costs) in its record quarter, so it can fund new factories and buybacks at once.
bear: Trefis found that after 8 past profit peaks since 2000, Micron's stock was lower a year later every time, by a typical 34.7%.
The stock fell 9.4% in three trading days through November 18 even with Nvidia's strong news, showing investors are nervous about AI spending.
The new November 16 US license rule on AI chip exports to five countries could slow AI chip sales, which would mean less memory needed.
briefs.nextEvent: Micron's next quarterly report, expected in late December 2026

briefs.name: Micron Technology
briefs.whyMoved: Micron closed at $705.27 on November 18, down from $712.42 on November 17 and 9.4% below its $778.31 close on November 13. After Nvidia reported $115.84 billion in quarterly sales on November 17, Micron rose as much as 3.5% before the market opened on November 18, but the gain faded as Nvidia itself slid 2.9% and the selling in AI stocks continued. Almost all of Micron's profit now comes from AI data centers, and Nvidia said its promises to buy parts jumped from $279 billion to $390 billion, mostly long deals for memory, which points to more orders for Micron. The worry is that Micron keeps a record 86.8 cents of gross profit on each sales dollar, and Trefis notes that after past profit peaks the stock was usually lower a year later, because memory prices tend to fall when supply catches up.

watch.what: Micron can start big stock buybacks. Fast buying would show the company thinks its stock is cheap; little buying would be a letdown.
Micron's next quarterly report. Good: a higher sales forecast and steady memory prices. Bad: a lower forecast or signs AI customers are slowing orders.

market.why: On Thursday, November 19, all four indexes fell about 2%, the Dow dropped 1,101 points, and the S&P 500 lost for a sixth day in a row. AI company Anthropic's record stock debut closed 17% above its $83 starting price, but it didn't cheer investors: Nvidia fell 3.3% and AMD sank 7.7%. Fears that the Fed will raise interest rates again in December, with prices still rising fast, hit big and small companies alike.
